findings.what_is_wrong: The refused set is narrower than the old rules M3 and M9 in three ways that neither the residual risk nor decisions/0102 item 15 names. (1) L2: an unquoted value counts as a secret only if it is a chain of [A-Za-z0-9+/=_~-]; everything else unquoted is 'an expression' and is stored. Run on the base clone: old maskSecrets hides DB_PASSWORD=P@ssw0rd!, SECRET=Sup3r!Secret#2026, password=Pa$$w0rd, token=ya29.a0AfH6SMBx1234567890abcdefghijk; by the written definition all four are stored. Residual (2) names only 'shorter than 8 or no digit'. (2) F3: a URL password containing $, { or < is not refused: old M3 hides https://deploy:Pa$$w0rd@example.com/x and https://deploy:p{ss}w0rd1@example.com/x; the text excludes the single characters $, {, < (L1 excludes only the pairs ${ and {{), so it is also inconsistent inside. (3) L1: a quoted value with < or > or ${ or {{ is an expression: old M9 hides password: "p<ss>w0rd", new keeps it. Real passwords contain these characters; the decision record and the README would not tell the owner. Step 9 cannot tell whether such values must be refused, and no sample (C or O) pins any of the three cases, so the m4 and m9 mutants cannot show a difference.
